## Overview

The **Arctic Weather Satellite (AWS)** is an ESA mission designed to improve
numerical weather prediction in the Arctic.
AWS-1 carries a 19-channel Microwave Radiometer (MWR) spanning frequencies
from ~23 GHz to ~183 GHz, enabling tropospheric temperature and humidity
profiling under all weather conditions.

The S3 bucket at `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/AWS/` holds Level 1B
radiance and brightness temperature products processed by KSAT (Kongsberg
Satellite Services) in Near-Real-Time (NRT) mode.

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| Satellite | AWS-1 |
| Agency | ESA |
| Instrument | Microwave Radiometer (MWR) |
| Channels | 19 |
| Processing level | 1B — antenna-corrected TOA brightness temperatures and radiances |
| Data format | NetCDF-4 (inside a ZIP archive; `.nc` extension) |
| S3 bucket | `s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/AWS/` |
| Date range in bucket | 2026-01-23 – 2026-02-18 |
| Total granules | 406 |
| Approx. total size | ~59 GB |

---

## S3 bucket organisation

Files are arranged under a `{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/` hierarchy:

```
s3://airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket/JOIN/AWS/
  2026/
    01/
      23/   ← 1 granule
      24/   ← 1 granule
      …
      31/
    02/
      01/   ← ~10–15 granules/day
      …
      18/
```

January coverage is sparse (1 granule per day); February coverage is denser
(10–15 granules per day, typically one ~90-minute orbit per file).

---

## File naming convention

Files follow the WMO/EUMETSAT standard filename format:

```
W_NO-KSAT-Tromso,SAT,AWS1-MWR-1B-RAD_C_OHB__{creation_ts}_G_O_{start_ts}_{end_ts}_C_N____.nc
```

### Example

```
W_NO-KSAT-Tromso,SAT,AWS1-MWR-1B-RAD_C_OHB__20260124121256_G_O_20260124102804_20260124120437_C_N____.nc
```

| Field | Example | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `W_NO-KSAT-Tromso` | — | WMO format; originating ground station (Tromsø, Norway) |
| `SAT,AWS1` | — | Platform: Arctic Weather Satellite 1 |
| `MWR-1B-RAD` | — | Instrument, processing level, product type |
| `20260124121256` | — | File creation time (UTC): 2026-01-24 12:12:56 |
| `20260124102804` | — | Sensing start time (UTC): 2026-01-24 10:28:04 |
| `20260124120437` | — | Sensing stop time (UTC): 2026-01-24 12:04:37 |

**Important:** Despite the `.nc` extension, each file is a **ZIP archive**
containing a NetCDF-4 data file plus `EOPMetadata.xml` and `manifest.xml`
sidecar files.
The NetCDF file inside must be extracted before opening.

---

## File contents

Each granule is a NetCDF-4 file with three top-level groups:
`status`, `data`, and `quality`.

```
/
├── status/
│   ├── satellite/   ← orbital elements, attitude errors
│   └── instrument/  ← channel frequencies, calibration coefficients, housekeeping
├── data/
│   ├── navigation/      ← per-FOV geolocation, angles, surface type
│   ├── measurement/     ← raw earth/cold/warm counts
│   └── calibration/     ← TOA brightness temperatures, radiances, calibration terms
│       processing_information/  ← per-scan and per-channel quality flags
└── quality/             ← summary quality flags, data coverage statistics
```

A typical granule covers ~90 minutes and contains
**4 866 scans × 145 FOVs/scan × 19 channels**.

### `status/satellite`

Orbital and attitude metadata.
Scalar values describe the epoch state vector; (n_fovs,) arrays give
per-FOV attitude error estimates.

| Variable | Shape | Dtype | Description | Units |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `epoch_time_utc` | () | float64 | UTC epoch of orbital elements | s since 2020-01-01 |
| `semi_major_axis` | () | float64 | Semi-major axis at epoch | m |
| `eccentricity` | () | float64 | Orbital eccentricity | — |
| `inclination` | () | float64 | Inclination at epoch | degrees |
| `perigee_argument` | () | float64 | Argument of perigee | degrees |
| `right_ascension` | () | float64 | Right ascension of ascending node | degrees |
| `mean_anomaly` | () | float64 | Mean anomaly at epoch | degrees |
| `earth_sun_distance_ratio` | () | float64 | Earth–Sun distance ratio | — |
| `subsat_latitude_start/end` | () | float64 | Sub-satellite latitude at granule start/end | degrees_north |
| `subsat_longitude_start/end` | () | float64 | Sub-satellite longitude at granule start/end | degrees_east |
| `state_vector_time_utc` | () | float64 | UTC time of orbit state vector | s since 2020-01-01 |
| `x/y/z_position` | () | float64 | ECEF spacecraft position components | m |
| `x/y/z_velocity` | () | float64 | ECEF spacecraft velocity components | m/s |
| `yaw_error` | (145,) | float64 | Yaw attitude error per FOV | degrees |
| `roll_error` | (145,) | float64 | Roll attitude error per FOV | degrees |
| `pitch_error` | (145,) | float64 | Pitch attitude error per FOV | degrees |
| `leap_second_time_utc` | () | float64 | Time of applicable leap second | s since 2020-01-01 |
| `leap_second_value` | () | int16 | Leap second value (+1/−1/0) | seconds |

Key dimensions: `n_scans` (4 866), `n_channels` (19), `n_fovs` (145).

| Variable | Shape | Description |

| `channel_central_freq` | (19,) | Central frequency of each channel (GHz) |
| `channel_bandwidths` | (19,) | Channel bandwidth (Hz) |
| `channel_central_wavenum` | (19,) | Central wavenumber (cm⁻¹) |
| `mirror_reflectivity_perpendicular` | (145, 19) | Per-FOV per-channel mirror reflectivity |
| `aws_thermistor` | (4866, 4) | Thermistor readings (counts) |
| `aws_prt` | (4866, 4) | Platinum resistance thermometer readings (counts) |
| `aws_sdss` | (4866, 19) | Sample data saturation status |
| `aws_sma_assembly_status` | (4866,) | Scan mechanism assembly status |

## Opening a file with Python

Because each `.nc` file is actually a ZIP archive, it must be extracted before
use.
The following snippet downloads a file from S3, extracts the inner NetCDF, and
opens it with xarray:

```python
import zipfile
import io
import xarray as xr
import obstore
from obstore.store import S3Store

S3_BUCKET = "airborne-smce-prod-user-bucket"
S3_REGION = "us-west-2"

key = ("JOIN/AWS/2026/01/24/"
       "W_NO-KSAT-Tromso,SAT,AWS1-MWR-1B-RAD_C_OHB__20260124121256"
       "_G_O_20260124102804_20260124120437_C_N____.nc")

store = S3Store.from_url(f"s3://{S3_BUCKET}/", region=S3_REGION)
raw = bytes(obstore.get(store, key).bytes())

# The .nc file is a ZIP archive — extract the inner NetCDF
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(raw)) as zf:
    nc_name = [n for n in zf.namelist() if n.endswith(".nc")][0]
    nc_bytes = zf.read(nc_name)

ds = xr.open_dataset(io.BytesIO(nc_bytes), group="data/calibration")
print(ds)
```

To access a specific group, pass the `group=` argument to `xr.open_dataset`
(e.g. `group="data/navigation"` for geolocation arrays,
`group="data/calibration"` for brightness temperatures).
